name: Arcade Fire
label: Merge
lede: A Montreal band that named its debut after the funerals it was living through, got a 9.7 from Pitchfork, sang with Bowie, beat Eminem for a Grammy, and then went disco with James Murphy.

eras.title: A fire in an arcade that never happened
eras.text: Win Butler, a Texan who'd gone to Phillips Exeter, starts a band in Montreal's Mile End with his school friend Josh Deu and a McGill student named Régine Chassagne. The first lineup falls apart in public, and the one that replaces it is the band the world will meet.

years.h: Win Butler and Josh Deu start Arcade Fire in Montreal
years.p: Win Butler and Josh Deu, friends from Phillips Exeter Academy, recruit Régine Chassagne at McGill plus Brendan Reed, Dane Mills, Myles Broscoe and Tim Kile.
years.xp:
Butler says the name comes from a story someone told him as a kid, about a fire in an arcade. He later decided the story was probably made up, but he believed it at the time.

That first Christmas the band recorded A Very Arcade Xmas and handed copies out as gifts.

years.h: Maine sessions: Myles Broscoe quits, Richard Reed Parry joins
years.p: Arcade Fire record their first EP on Mount Desert Island, Maine. Myles Broscoe leaves after tensions with Win Butler, [[Richard Reed Parry|ebb15840-19c5-4c4b-98b1-4cddeb4d7684]] joins mid-session, and Josh Deu goes back to school.

years.h: Arcade Fire break up onstage at Casa del Popolo
years.p: A Casa del Popolo show in Montreal ends in an onstage argument between Win Butler and drummer Brendan Reed. Reed quits on the spot and Dane Mills tells the crowd the band has broken up.
years.xp: It hadn't, quite. Butler and Régine Chassagne kept going, and within months had a new rhythm section: Win's younger brother [[Will Butler|928b0e29-31d2-4c67-8377-ec93d24721b3]] and bassist [[Tim Kingsbury|a609b901-2d94-43f7-8456-8f638667a717]]. Engineer [[Howard Bilerman|39450b35-6fbc-453a-9f78-d295999617bd]] took over the drums that summer.

years.h: Will Butler and Tim Kingsbury replace Brendan Reed and Dane Mills
years.p: Win Butler's younger brother Will Butler and bassist Tim Kingsbury join Arcade Fire, and Hotel2Tango co-owner Howard Bilerman starts drumming for them in the summer.

years.h: Arcade Fire EP, sold at Montreal shows
years.p: The Maine recordings come out as a self-released EP, the first place No Cars Go appears. Merge reissues the Arcade Fire EP in 2005 once the world is paying attention.

eras.title: Four funerals and a 9.7
eras.text: Arcade Fire made their first album while three families in the band were burying people. It came out on Merge Records, a small label in Chapel Hill, and one review turned it into the record every indie fan owned by Christmas.

years.h: Funeral on Merge, named for three families' losses
years.p: Arcade Fire's debut album is recorded mostly in August 2003 at Hotel2Tango in Montreal for about $10,000. Merge releases Funeral on September 14, 2004.
years.xp:
The title is literal. Régine Chassagne's grandmother died in June 2003. Win and Will Butler's grandfather, the swing bandleader Alvino Rey, died in February 2004. Richard Reed Parry lost two aunts in April 2004.

According to Wikipedia, Funeral had sold more than 500,000 copies by November 2005 and nearly 750,000 by March 2007. It went gold in the US, platinum in the UK and double platinum in Canada.

years.h: Pitchfork gives Funeral a 9.7
years.p: Pitchfork's 9.7 review of Arcade Fire's Funeral is widely credited with breaking the album. The site later ranked it No. 2 of the whole 2000s.

years.h: Arcade Fire on the cover of Time's Canadian edition
years.p: Seven months after Funeral, Arcade Fire are on the cover of Time magazine's Canadian edition.

years.cap: Arcade Fire at Madison Square Garden, 2010 · Wikimedia
years.h: [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]] sings Wake Up with Arcade Fire
years.p: David Bowie, an early fan, performs with Arcade Fire several times in 2005, including Fashion Rocks on September 9. Their versions of Wake Up, Five Years and Life on Mars? are sold on iTunes.
years.xp: It was the start of a long friendship. Eight years later Bowie sang backing vocals on the title track of Reflektor, after telling the band he loved it.

years.h: Arcade Fire start giving to Haiti, Régine Chassagne's family's homeland
years.p: Régine Chassagne's parents came from Haiti. From 2005 Arcade Fire funnel money to Partners in Health there, later adding a surcharge on every ticket.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band added a dollar, pound or euro to tickets for Partners in Health and KANPE, the Haitian foundation Chassagne co-founded. The NFL licensed Wake Up for Super Bowl XLIV in 2010, and the proceeds went to Partners in Health too.

eras.title: A church in Farnham
eras.text: With money and time for the first time, Arcade Fire bought a disused church outside Montreal and made a darker, louder record inside it. Neon Bible leaked six weeks early and still went to No. 2 in America.

years.h: Arcade Fire turn a church in Farnham, Quebec, into a studio
years.p: Arcade Fire buy a disused church in Farnham, about 70 km southeast of Montreal, and convert it into the studio where they make Neon Bible.
years.xp: The church served the band until January 2013, when they announced they were selling it because the roof had collapsed.

years.h: Neon Bible leaks five weeks before release
years.p: Arcade Fire's second album, Neon Bible, hits peer-to-peer networks on January 26, 2007.

years.h: Arcade Fire's first Saturday Night Live
years.p: Arcade Fire make their SNL debut, playing Intervention and Keep the Car Running. It's the first of seven SNL appearances through 2025.

years.h: Neon Bible debuts at No. 2 in the US
years.p: Recorded in the Farnham church, Neon Bible opens at No. 1 in Canada and Ireland and No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and in the UK.
years.xp: Intervention, with the church's pipe organ all over it, had come out on iTunes in December 2006 with the proceeds going to Partners in Health. The Neon Bible tour ran to 122 shows in 75 cities in 19 countries before ending in February 2008.

years.h: Arcade Fire play free shows for Barack Obama
years.p: Win Butler campaigns for Barack Obama, and Arcade Fire play free concerts in Ohio in March 2008 and North Carolina in May before those states' primaries.
years.xp: In January 2009 Arcade Fire and Jay-Z were the musical guests at the Obama campaign staff ball at the D.C. Armory.

eras.title: Who is Arcade Fire?
eras.text: The Suburbs went back to the Butler brothers' Houston suburb and went to No. 1 in four countries. Then it beat Eminem, Katy Perry and Lady Gaga for the biggest Grammy there is, and a lot of TV viewers had never heard of the winners.

years.h: The Suburbs: a letter from The Woodlands, Texas
years.p: Arcade Fire's third album looks back at Win and Will Butler's childhood in The Woodlands, a Houston suburb. The Suburbs debuts at No. 1 in the US, UK, Canada and Ireland.
years.xp:
Win Butler described it as a letter from the suburbs, neither love letter nor attack. The US first week came to 156,000 units, per Wikipedia.

The Wilderness Downtown, an interactive video made with Google and director Chris Milk for We Used to Wait, asked viewers for the address they grew up at and built the video around it.

years.cap: Arcade Fire at Razzmatazz, Barcelona, 2016 · Wikimedia
years.h: The Suburbs wins the Grammy for Album of the Year
years.p: Arcade Fire beat Eminem, Katy Perry, Lady Gaga and Lady Antebellum. They accept, then play Ready to Start as the broadcast rolls on.
years.xp:
A Tumblr called Who Is Arcade Fire?!!! collected baffled posts from viewers who'd never heard of the band, and it became part of the story of the night.

The run kept going: Best International Album at the BRITs two days later, Album of the Year at the Junos, and the Polaris Music Prize in September.

years.h: Spike Jonze's Scenes from the Suburbs premieres in Berlin
years.p: Spike Jonze's 30-minute film built on Arcade Fire's The Suburbs premieres at the Berlin International Film Festival and screens at SXSW in March.

eras.title: Dress code: formal attire or costume
eras.text: Arcade Fire went disco with James Murphy, played secret shows in disguise, and asked arena crowds to dress up. By Everything Now they'd left Merge for Columbia and built a whole fake corporation around the record, and not everyone got the joke.

years.h: Arcade Fire sell the Farnham church after its roof collapses
years.p: The Quebec church where Arcade Fire made Neon Bible goes up for sale; the band says the roof has collapsed.

years.h: Arcade Fire play secret Montreal shows as The Reflektors
years.p: Before Reflektor comes out, Arcade Fire play small club shows in Montreal under the fake name The Reflektors, with the crowd told to come in costume or formal wear.

years.h: Arcade Fire's SNL special with Bono, Ben Stiller and Bill Hader
years.p: Arcade Fire open SNL's 39th season, then NBC airs Here Comes the Night Time, a special with cameos from Bono, Ben Stiller, Bill Hader and Zach Galifianakis.

years.h: Reflektor: James Murphy, Haiti and Bowie on the title track
years.p: Produced with Markus Dravs and LCD Soundsystem's [[James Murphy|6b70c46c-5c83-4cc7-99c1-e76b68919c6a]], Reflektor is a double album drawing on Haitian rara. David Bowie sings on the title track.
years.xp: Kahlil Joseph's film The Reflektor Tapes followed the making of it and premiered at the 2015 Toronto International Film Festival. Reflektor won the 2014 Juno for Album of the Year.

years.h: Arcade Fire ask arena crowds for formal wear or costumes
years.p: Tickets for the 2014 Reflektor arena tour request formal attire or a costume. Critics grumble; the band's reply amounts to please relax.

years.h: Will Butler and Owen Pallett get an Oscar nomination for Her
years.p: Will Butler and [[Owen Pallett|6d394418-a565-4c16-9dec-f5a89e213cde]] are nominated for Best Original Score at the 86th Academy Awards for Spike Jonze's Her, scored with Arcade Fire.

years.h: Everything Now, Arcade Fire's first record for Columbia
years.p: After signing a two-album deal with Columbia in May 2017, Arcade Fire release Everything Now. The title track becomes their first No. 1 on Billboard's Adult Alternative chart.
years.xp: The single was first sold as a limited 12-inch at Primavera Sound in Barcelona on May 31. In October 2017 the band parted ways with its longtime manager, Scott Rodger.

years.h: Arcade Fire publish a fake Stereogum review of their own album
years.p: To promote Everything Now, the band's fictional Everything Now Corp. posts a spoof of Stereogum's Premature Evaluation column reviewing the record, one of a string of fake-news stunts.

eras.title: WE, and Will goes
eras.text: Will Butler quietly left after finishing WE, the band's second record for Columbia. It came out in May 2022, and Arcade Fire toured it through the rest of the year.

years.h: Will Butler leaves Arcade Fire after finishing WE
years.p: Will Butler leaves on good terms once WE is done. The departure isn't made public until 2022.

years.h: WE, and a closing shout for abortion rights on SNL
years.p: Arcade Fire release WE on May 6. Playing SNL the next night, Win Butler closes the set with a call for abortion rights.

q: has been mutual and always between consenting adults
years.src: Pitchfork · Variety · The FADER · Wikipedia · CBC · Global News
years.h: Win Butler faces sexual misconduct allegations
years.p: In August 2022 Pitchfork reported that four people accused Win Butler of sexual misconduct between 2015 and 2020. Butler said every encounter was consensual.
years.xp:
Three women, aged 18 to 23 at the time, told Pitchfork the relationships were inappropriate given the age and power gap. A fourth person, who is gender-fluid, said Butler sexually assaulted them twice in 2015. Butler acknowledged the encounters and denied the misconduct; Régine Chassagne issued her own statement backing him.

[[Feist|a670e05a-cea8-4b37-bce9-d82daf1a0fa4]] quit as opener on the European leg of the WE tour after two shows and gave her proceeds to a Dublin women's aid group; Beck later withdrew from the North American leg. CBC reported some radio stations stopped playing the band. In November a fifth woman told Pitchfork her three-year relationship with Butler, begun in 2015 when she was 22, was abusive; Butler again said it was consensual.

eras.title: Pink Elephant
eras.text: Arcade Fire came back on their own terms: a surprise app, a short tour, a record with Daniel Lanois. Months later, Win Butler and Régine Chassagne said their marriage was over; the band kept going.

years.h: Pink Elephant, announced through the band's own app
years.p: Arcade Fire tease the album through an app called Trust, debut songs at Luck Reunion in Texas, and release Pink Elephant on May 9.
years.xp:
The nine-show tour that followed ran from Mexico City on April 22 to London on May 14, with pay-what-you-can pricing at three benefit shows in New Orleans and New York. Richard Reed Parry sat it out because his wife was about to give birth.

The day after release they played SNL for the seventh time.

years.h: Win Butler and Régine Chassagne announce their separation
years.p: Married since 2003 and the band's two constants since 2001, Win Butler and Régine Chassagne announce on Instagram that they have separated.

years.h: Open Your Heart or Die Trying, an ambient Arcade Fire album
years.p: Arcade Fire announce an ambient companion record, released as a Record Store Day exclusive on April 18 and on streaming May 1.
